title: Secure audit egress to customer-controlled storage with on-prem compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide a secure, robust mechanism for forwarding audit events from Private/VPC/on-prem Redwood Inference installations to customer-managed storage backends (S3/GCS/Azure/MinIO/SFTP) while preserving integrity, supporting large multipart uploads, and meeting enterprise compliance requirements.
background: Customers deploying Redwood in private networks require the ability to store audit logs in locations they control for compliance (CIS/HIPAA) and retention policies. Existing hosted audit exporters are insufficient for air-gapped or customer-managed storage scenarios. Previous tickets explored adapters and forwarders, but customers need a unified pattern with clear auth, integrity checks, retry semantics, and operational controls.
scope: Design and implement an extensible egress component that runs in the Private control plane or adjacent operator and can: 1) authenticate to customer storage using presigned URLs, short-lived credentials, or connector-specific tokens; 2) upload large audit batches with resumable/multipart uploads; 3) verify successful delivery and provide provenance metadata; 4) expose observability and error handling; 5) support S3/GCS/Azure/MinIO and on-prem SFTP/HTTP endpoints.
non_goals: Building a generic SIEM connector or long-term log indexing. We will not re-implement full object-store drivers for every vendor—use existing SDKs or lightweight shim connectors. We will not provide a hosted long-term retention service in this ticket.
proposed_solution: Introduce 'egress-handoff', a small, pluggable service that: (a) accepts batched audit payloads from the control plane over a local, authenticated channel; (b) converts them to compressed, chunked objects and uploads to target storage; (c) maintains a signed manifest per upload containing SHA256 checksums and uploader metadata; (d) supports connector modes: presigned, assume-role (AWS STS), GCP service account impersonation, Azure SAS, and token-based for on-prem MinIO/SFTP; (e) tracks progress in a local persisted queue with durable checkpoints and a DLQ for permanent failures.
design_decisions: Use connector abstraction so vendor-specific auth is implemented in small adapters rather than core code
Leverage presigned URLs where possible to avoid storing long-lived secrets inside customer deployments
Keep manifests as JSON lines with base64-encoded signature to preserve backwards readability
Implement multipart uploads for S3/GCS to handle >100MB payloads and avoid OOMs
Default to server-side encryption (SSE) option but provide CMEK handshake guidance for customers who require KMS-managed keys
auth_patterns: Supported auth flows: AWS assume-role with STS + short-lived creds; presigned PUT URLs generated by customer-owned control plane or via a configured operator; GCP service account impersonation + signed URLs; Azure SAS tokens; on-prem token + TLS client certs for MinIO/SFTP. For manually-managed air-gapped setups, allow operator to accept mounted credentials via filesystem with strict RBAC and file permission checks.
integrity_checks: Each upload produces a manifest file that enumerates object parts with byte ranges and SHA256 checksums. The egress agent signs the manifest using the cluster's signing key and stores signature metadata in object metadata. Customers can optionally enable HMAC verification using a pre-shared key or request signed manifests for third-party verification.
operational_controls: Backpressure: configurable max in-flight uploads and queue size. Retries: exponential backoff with jitter and configurable max attempts. DLQ: on fatal errors (403/401/unsupported endpoint) events land in a local disk-based DLQ and a high-severity alert is emitted. Metrics: uploads_success, uploads_failed, bytes_transferred, average_latency, queue_depth. Tracing hooks for request provenance linked to trace IDs in audit events.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge connector interface and CI tests behind feature flag; 2) Deploy egress-handoff to a small set of internal private clusters as canary; 3) Validate uploads to test customer-managed buckets (internal harness); 4) Open beta with 3 pilot customers under SE guidance; 5) General availability after 2 weeks of successful pilots and completing security review.
acceptance_criteria: egress-handoff runs in Private/VPC and accepts audit batches via local API
Successfully uploads 10GB multipart test payload to S3/GCS/Azure and verifies manifest checksums
Supports at least two auth modes (presigned URLs and STS assume-role) end-to-end
DLQ behavior triggers for unreachable endpoints and generates a telemetry alert
Documentation and operator runbook published with KMS/CMEK guidance
test_plan: Unit tests for connector adapters and manifest signing. Integration tests with AWS/GCP/Azure emulators (localstack, fake-gcs-server) for multipart flows. Chaos test: simulate network interruption mid-multipart and assert resumability and manifest consistency. Security fuzzing around credential parsing and TLS handling.
risks: Credential leakage if connectors incorrectly persist long-lived secrets
Edge-case mismatch between multipart implementations across vendors causing partial objects
Customer-configured retention/policy mismatches leading to audit disappearance
Latency spikes when large backlog and burst uploads coincide causing downstream throttling
mitigations: Never persist long-lived credentials; prefer short-lived tokens and presigned flows
Implement part hash verification and atomic manifest finalize step
Provide a retention-check tool in the operator to validate bucket lifecycle settings
Throttle uploader and provide adaptive batching; surface clear SLOs to customers
notes: Design review scheduled 2025-02-16 with Security and Product; initial feedback requested on manifest signing format
PM asked to prioritize AWS and GCS for pilot customers; Azure and SFTP scheduled for GA+1
Coordinate with infra for operator RBAC roles and K8s PSPs for mounted credential volumes
